1.why: Reset validation requires token === session.resetToken for the caller’s session after that session requested the reset.

2.why: The reset token is stored only on the requesting session, so another user’s session has no matching resetToken and cannot use it.

3.why: password-update only mutates the current session and never invalidates or removes other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS certs and non-HTTPS is rejected, but the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens and session fields are stored in memory in plaintext, not encrypted.

6.why: There is no real email body; API copy is generic and does not include profile PII beyond the demo mock token channel.

7.why: Email/token/password inputs are type-checked and validated, and the UI builds nodes with textContent rather than injecting HTML.

8.why: No user-controlled redirect targets exist; navigation is in-app screen changes and fetch calls to same-origin /api paths.

9.why: There are no email templates that interpolate user input into HTML or scripts; delivery is only simulated locally.

10.why: Server error JSON is generic with no stack traces, but the UI logs panel deliberately prints reset and MFA tokens.

11.why: MFA_CODE is hardcoded as "482913" in source; only the password is stored via bcrypt on the session.

12.why: There is no default password login path and new passwords must meet a strong policy, though the demo MFA secret is fixed.

13.why: rateAllowed throttles reset-request (3/15m), reset-validate (5/15m), and mfa-verify (5/15m) attempts per session.

14.why: reset-request always returns the same generic message and a mock token whether or not the email is the known account.

15.why: reset tokens are 32-byte crypto random base64url values stored on the requesting session, hence complex and session-specific.
